meta: Estimate your LESCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. Lahore protected units explained.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the LESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: LESCO, the Lahore Electric Supply Company, does not set its own rates. It bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026, the same slabs as every other DISCO. For an unprotected home the rate of the slab the month's units reach applies to every unit: 300 units are all billed at Rs 33.10, the top slab is the most expensive, and the first hundred units are the cheapest.

The worked examples below print the rate for the protected, the 300-unit, the 500-unit and the lifeline cases, and the table lists the rate for each slab. The FPA is pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified month; replace it with your bill's for the exact figure.

LESCO marks a domestic consumer as protected when all of the last 6 bills were at or under 200 units and the connection is below 5 kW. Protected bills use two low slabs and are billed slab-wise, with the first hundred units at the first rate and the rest at the second.
A single month above 200 units, including one stretched by a long reading cycle, moves the home to unprotected rates for every unit. Tick the protected box only when the bill itself says protected.

sections.h2: LESCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the LESCO site
p: This page is a LESCO bill estimate from your units. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the LESCO website; use it to pay and to see the printed lines. Use this calculator to understand what each line should be, to plan next month's bill, or to check a bill that looks too high against the slab it should fall in.

For the full version of this tool with every DISCO and a longer explanation of the slabs, see the electricity bill calculator for Pakistan. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means.

If a bill looks too high, run it through the bill overbilling check, and see this month's bill at every level of units in the Pakistan electricity bill index. Before adding an appliance, check your connection with the sanctioned load calculator and what one AC adds to the bill with the AC bill calculator.

faq.q: How do I get a LESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from your bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and the estimate shows energy, fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST. For 300 units the estimate is Rs 14,186.

faq.q: What is the LESCO per unit price?
faq.a: It is the NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches. An unprotected home using 300 units pays Rs 33.10 per unit; the table above gives the rate for each slab, and protected homes pay far less.

faq.q: Is the LESCO unit price the same as other DISCOs?
faq.a: Yes. The 2026 tariff is uniform for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. NEPRA sets one monthly FPA for every DISCO too, so the same units give the same bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: What is the LESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to 100 units, protected slabs up to 200 units and unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700, then an open-ended top slab; connections of 5 kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

faq.q: How do I check my LESCO bill online?
faq.a: The official LESCO bill check is on the LESCO website, where the reference number on your bill brings up the current bill and payment status. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your bill.

LESCO supplies the districts of Lahore, Kasur, Okara, Sheikhupura and Nankana Sahib. Faults and billing complaints go to the national electricity helpline 118 (call, or SMS 8118); the official bill, with its reference number, is on the LESCO website.

faq.q: How many units keep a LESCO consumer protected?
faq.a: At or under 200 units in every one of the last 6 months, on a connection below 5 kW. Cross the limit once and the next bills are unprotected until six months under the limit have passed again.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: LESCO charges the NEPRA uniform A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, so a LESCO bill for a given number of units is the same as any other DISCO's, FPA included, because NEPRA sets one FPA for every company.
The LESCO per unit rate for an unprotected home using 300 units is Rs 33.10 on every unit, which gives Rs 9,930 before the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.
LESCO protected units: a home stays protected only while every one of its last 6 bills is at or under 200 units; protected bills are worked out slab-wise at much lower rates.
GST at 18% is charged on energy, fixed charge and surcharges together, adding Rs 2,164 to a 300 unit LESCO bill; the surcharge and GST values are secondary-source figures that change monthly.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,481 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Looking for a separate LESCO tariff. LESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic tariff; the slab rates are the same across Pakistan.
Assuming last month's protected status still holds. One bill over 200 units moves you to unprotected rates for every unit.
Keeping the pre-filled FPA when the bill shows a different one. The fuel adjustment line can swing the total either way; copy your bill's rate into the advanced field.
Dividing the total bill by units to get a per unit rate. The fixed charge, surcharges and GST are mixed in; the slab rate is the energy charge divided by units.

fields.label: Units on the LESCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill; most Lahore homes are one to five. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick if every one of your last six LESCO bills was within the protected unit limit; the bill prints the category.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

content.answer: A LESCO home using 300 units a month as an unprotected consumer on a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 14,186, of which Rs 9,930 is the energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit and the rest is fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. LESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges + GST.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the bill
